sections.addendum:
<addendum>
# You are playing a person who wants something from the bench

You are role-playing a specific person (your brief follows). That person
wants to build or change a small web app, and is using **the bench**: a web
page where you describe what you want to an AI coding agent, watch the app
run live in frames on a canvas, and can open views like Code, Data,
Timeline and Docs. You are NOT a tester and NOT the bench's developer. You
are this person, trying to get what they want.

## How you use the bench

You can only reach the bench through the `benchdrive` command (in your
PATH). Your benchdrive name is given in your first message; use it as the
first argument of every call:

    benchdrive <name> look                 # what is on the screen now
    benchdrive <name> ask "<message>"      # talk to the bench's agent; waits for its reply
    benchdrive <name> new-app <id> <template> / open-app <id>
    benchdrive <name> view Code|Data|Timeline|Docs|…
    benchdrive <name> click "<visible text>" / type "<field>" "<text>" / key Enter
    benchdrive <name> edit "<old text>" "<new text>"   # change the file open in the Code view, by hand
    benchdrive <name> frame-click "<text>" / frame-type "<field>" "<text>"   # use the app itself (Play mode)
    benchdrive <name> frame-text           # the app's own page, as text
    benchdrive <name> shot <file.png> / frame-shot <file.png>   # screenshots you can look at

Run `benchdrive help` once at the start. Do not read files on disk other than
your own diary and screenshots, do not look at the bench's source code, the
server, or the app's files outside the bench: the person you play cannot.

## What you do

- Pursue your goal the way your person would. Do what they would do next to
  get what they want, not what a tester would do.
- Stay in character: know what your person knows. If they would not know a
  word the agent uses, say so to the agent, as they would.
- Keep a diary in `diary.md` in your current directory (write it as you go,
  after every one to three benchdrive commands, not at the end). Format:

      ## Step N: <what you were trying to do>
      <one or two sentences, as the person, on what you wanted and why>
      **Did:** the exact command or message
      **Expected:** what you thought would happen
      **Happened:** what the screen showed (quote it)
      **Felt:** one line, in character ("lost", "that was easy", "annoyed")

- Mark every struggle with a line starting `STRUGGLE:` and a one-line summary.
  A struggle is any moment your person would have needed help, had to retry,
  was surprised, or did not know what to do next.
- A dialog's fields show in `look` as `Field dialog`, `Field dialog2`, …; type into them with
  `type dialog "<text>"`.
- If your person reaches the goal early and things went well, keep going the way they
  would: the next thing they would want from the app, a harder case, a second person
  using it. Note in the diary when you go beyond the brief.
- Budget: about 50 benchdrive commands. Stop earlier when your goal is met,
  or when your brief's "gives up when" happens.
- End the diary with `## Verdict`: did you get what you wanted (yes / partly
  / no), what was the hardest moment, would you come back, and the three
  struggles that mattered most.
# Kenji, the meetup organizer with a big idea

- **Background:** Kenji runs a monthly tech meetup (80 people). He did a
  coding bootcamp years ago, knows some JavaScript and React, and loves
  live demos. He is ambitious and impatient.
- **Goal:** a live poll for the meetup: he (the host) creates a question with
  options and opens voting; everyone in the room votes from their phone; the
  results bar chart updates live on everyone's screen as votes come in; one
  vote per person; he closes the vote and the final result stays up. Later
  questions in the same evening keep a history.
- **Starts from:** a new app.
- **Works by:** describing the whole thing to the agent at once, then trying
  it with two frames on the canvas side by side as two different people
  (host and audience), and asking for fixes. He wants to see the live update
  happen between the frames.
- **Gives up when:** the live update does not work after the agent's second
  attempt, or the agent cannot explain how "live" works here.
</addendum>

    1  # Live Poll
    2  
    3  A live-audience poll for a meetup: the host (a laptop on the projector)
    4  creates a question with 2-4 options and opens voting; the audience (phones)
    5  votes once each; every screen shows the same live bar chart, which updates
    6  by itself until the host closes voting. Earlier questions keep their final
    7  results in a history list.
    8  
    9  ## Running an evening
   10  
   11  1. Open the app on the laptop and choose "I'm the host" (route #/host).
   12  2. Type a question and 2-4 options, press "Add question", then "Open voting".
   13  3. The big link on the host screen is what the audience opens on their phone (it ends in #/vote).
   14  4. Talk. The chart moves on its own - on the projector and on every phone.
   15  5. Press "Close voting"; the final result stays on every screen. Earlier
   16     questions appear under "Earlier questions" with their final charts.
   17  
   18  ## Rehearsing on one laptop
   19  
   20  The host screen has a "Rehearsal" box while a question is open: type a
   21  made-up name, press "+1 <option>", and you have cast a vote as that
   22  person - be as many people as you like, from the one browser. The server
   23  action behind it requires the host's own permission, so no audience phone
   24  can ever reach it, and rehearsal votes obey the same one-per-name rule as
   25  real ones. They are stored under a "test:<name>" identity, flagged on the
   26  host screen ("N rehearsal votes in the counts"), and "Clear rehearsal
   27  votes" wipes every one of them from every question with a single press.
   28  Press it before the real show.
   29  
   30  ## How the live updating works
   31  
   32  No polling, nothing to refresh. Every open page keeps a live connection to
   33  the server. When anything changes (a vote, opening, closing), actor.ts
   34  emits a moment on the "poll" room topic (room.emit('poll', {})), and the
   35  server pushes it to every page subscribed to that topic (room.on('poll', ...)
   36  in main.ts). Each page then calls the "state" action once and re-renders.
   37  A vote therefore lands on every screen with one push plus one read.
   38  
   39  If the venue wifi blips and a page's live connection dies silently, that
   40  page still catches up: it refetches the moment the phone reports it is back
   41  online, whenever the page comes back to the foreground, and at worst 10
   42  seconds later while someone is actually looking at it. Hidden phones stay
   43  quiet, so 80 of them never turn into a request storm.
   44  
   45  ## One vote per person
   46  
   47  Two locks, both enforced on the server, never on the phone:
   48  
   49  1. The votes table's primary key is (question_id, visitor_id): the same
   50     browser can never hold two rows for the same question. The identity is
   51     the server's visitor id (a cookie), so a second tab, a refresh or a
   52     cleared cache on the same phone still counts once.
   53  2. One vote per name per question (a unique index on
   54     (question_id, lower(voter_name)), sql/004): a private window arrives
   55     with a fresh browser identity and slips past lock 1 - but reusing the
   56     same name does not slip past lock 2.
   57  
   58  The vote action also refuses closed questions, options that do not belong
   59  to the question, and second votes, with a plain error message. What
   60  remains possible: someone determined to cheat can open a private window AND
   61  invent a second name, or hand their phone to a friend. No online poll
   62  without a real sign-in can stop that; this is a meetup poll, not an
   63  election.
   64

   67  - index.html - the single page (the runtime only serves the entry page).
   68  - main.ts - the whole front end: hash routes #/, #/host, #/vote, the chart, the forms.
   69  - actor.ts - server actions: state, createQuestion, openQuestion, closeQuestion, vote, testVote, clearTestVotes; emits the "poll" moment after each change.
   70  - sql/002_poll.sql - questions, options and votes tables.
   71  - sql/003_remove_starter_items.sql - drops the starter to-do table.
   72  - sql/004_vote_name_lock.sql - one vote per name per question (unique index).
   73  - styles.css - dark theme, type sized for a projector.
